key_insight: RareDx improves rare-disease ranking by combining controlled evidence use with graph-grounded policy optimization so the model relies more on structured medical knowledge than on unconstrained generation.
clinical_relevance: This could help decision support systems surface rarer diagnoses more reliably in long-tail cases, but it is a research system rather than a clinical tool.
method: RareDx-Harness standardizes heterogeneous inputs into a shared ranked-diagnosis evaluation across multiple reasoning modes.
RareDx-KGPO trains with rewards based on canonical disease-graph projection, relevance, ontology proximity, biomedical similarity, and phenotype consistency.
Vocabulary and output-budget constraints are used to reduce fabricated or overly long differential diagnoses.
evidence_signal: Across eight benchmarks, the Qwen3.5-9B-based system achieved 38.34 macro Hit@10, and a held-out audit showed a 6.80-point routing gain over Direct.
watch_item: Performance depends on benchmark setup, canonical graph mapping, and controlled routing, so real-world clinical deployment would need careful validation on local data and workflows.
paper_title: RareDx: Controlled Knowledge Integration and Graph-Grounded Policy Optimization for Rare-Disease Diagnosis
